content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then fails to correct downward.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true price peaks, often missing 1–2 days of peak values.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts too aggressively revert to prior mean, ignoring recent trend persistence.
- Underestimates volatility in the final 5–7 days of the horizon, leading to underprediction of price surges.
- Overconfident in short-term forecasts (first 5–7 days) when actual price movements are more volatile than modeled.
- Fails to account for “rebound” after sharp declines — often underpredicts recovery in the 10–15 day window.
